criteria.criterion: `athena land --pr <job>` exists in the CLI. It pushes only the job's work branch (through `check_push`, never forced), opens a PR, reads check status, and stores a `PrLink` in the job's state directory.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: main.rs adds `Command::Land { job, pr (required), json }`, which calls `Athena::land_pr`. In gh.rs, `publish` calls `check_push` with `allowed_branch = work_branch(job)`, then `remote.push` (a plain `git push <remote> commit:refs/heads/branch` with no force), then `open_pr` and `store_link`. After that `land_pr` waits for the checks and stores the link again.

criteria.criterion: The host client in crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs runs only `gh api` REST calls (paths like repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls). It has no `gh pr` subcommands, no `graphql` endpoint, and no GraphQL query text.
criteria.evidence: `GhClient::api` always builds `["api","--method",M,path]`. The only paths used are repos/{repo}/pulls, pulls/{n}, commits/{sha}/check-runs, commits/{sha}/status and pulls/{n}/merge. A case-insensitive search of gh.rs for graphql or `gh pr` found only the text "gh printed" and a test assertion that rules out "pr". The test `the_client_runs_only_gh_api_with_rest_paths` checks this.

criteria.criterion: A new boolean setting enables merging via REST. It defaults to false when absent from the config. athena.toml is not changed, or if it is, the criterion naming it says why.
criteria.evidence: config.rs adds `Landing { #[serde(default)] merge_via_rest: bool }`, and `Config` marks it `#[serde(default)]`. The test `rest_merge_is_off_unless_the_config_turns_it_on` passed. `git diff HEAD~1 --stat -- athena.toml` printed nothing, so athena.toml is unchanged.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`. A test with a fake host shows that with the setting off (the default) no merge request is issued and the command ends with an open, green PR. A second test shows that with the setting on the REST merge call is issued.
criteria.evidence: `with_the_setting_off_no_merge_is_requested_and_the_pull_request_stays_open_and_green` passed (merges == 0, Open, Green). `with_the_setting_on_and_green_checks_the_rest_merge_is_requested_and_the_job_lands` passed (merges == 1). `the_client_runs_only_gh_api_with_rest_paths` checks that the merge is a PUT to repos/example/project/pulls/7/merge.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`. A test shows that when the PR is later seen merged, `check_merged` runs and the job is landed on a matching fingerprint, or `merged-unverified` otherwise. The merged commit is found by PR number, never by reading trailers.
criteria.evidence: `a_merge_seen_later_is_found_by_number_and_checked_by_content` passed. It covers both outcomes: Landed on a matching fingerprint and MergedUnverified on a different one, and it confirms the host was asked about PR 42. `observe_merge` calls `check_merged`. `GhClient::merged_commit` reads `pulls/{n}` `merge_commit_sha` and never reads trailers.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`. A test shows that red or pending checks never trigger a merge, even with the setting on.
criteria.evidence: `red_or_pending_checks_never_trigger_a_merge_even_with_the_setting_on` passed. It runs with the setting on and Red or Pending checks and asserts merges == 0. It also asserts that pending checks are read at most `attempts` times.

criteria.criterion: No email address outside the `email_allow` list in athena.toml appears in any changed file, including tests and fixtures. Use `noreply@`, `@example.com` or similar, or avoid emails entirely, e.g. no `user@host` strings in gh.rs.
criteria.evidence: An email-pattern search found no match in gh.rs. In the other changed Rust files the only match is a test line already in pr.rs before this change (pr.rs:394, an @example.com address), outside the added lines. The added lines in CHANGELOG.md, README.md and the design doc (read in the diff) contain no '@'. The remote fixtures use `github.com:example/project.git` with no user part.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. All pass.
criteria.evidence: I ran all three chained with &&, and the chain completed without error. The visible test output shows tests passing and no failures.

findings.summary: A landing is saved only in the PrLink state file, not as a job outcome record, so other views of the job (such as `athena status`) may not show it as landed.
findings.evidence: `land_pr` updates `link.state` through `observe_merge` and calls `store_link`. Nothing writes an `Outcome { state: OutcomeState::Landed }` record, which run.rs uses for other landings.

findings.summary: The setting is read from the repository's athena.toml at HEAD, so turning it on means editing a governance file. The docs call it 'the user's opt-in setting'.
The CLI's output text and exit-code mapping for `land --pr` have no tests.
findings.evidence: `display::land_pr` and `land_pr_code` were added, but the change adds no tests for them in athena-cli.

summary: The change does what was asked, so the verdict is pass. `athena land <job> --pr` now exists. It pushes only the job's branch `athena/<job>` (through `check_push`, with no force option), opens a pull request, waits for the checks and saves a `PrLink` in the job's state directory. The host client in gh.rs makes only `gh api` REST calls. The merge call runs only when the new `[landing] merge_via_rest` setting is on (it is off when missing) and the checks are green. With the setting off, the command stops at an open, green pull request. Running it again finds the merge by the pull request number and runs the merged-content check. No changed line contains an email address or GraphQL text, and athena.toml is unchanged. I ran fmt, clippy and the full test suite: all passed, including the 8 new gh.rs tests and the new config test. Three minor gaps: a landing is saved only in the link file, not as a job outcome record; turning the setting on means editing athena.toml, which is a governance file; and the CLI's printed output and exit-code mapping have no tests.
